page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 12 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation. It is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. The server integrates a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU with 80 GB of dedicated VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results indicate strong capabilities in specific workloads. The system achieves top-tier performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.51 GB/sec and strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 35.51 GB/sec. Large-block memory bandwidth is measured at 167.89 GB/sec for read-only operations and 74.22 GB/sec for write operations. In LLM inference benchmarks using a small 135M model, the server demonstrates top-tier efficiency, processing prompts at 10515.12 tokens/sec and generating text at 547.27 tokens/sec. Standard CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng and PassMark, register in the average range.

The server's hardware profile presents distinct tradeoffs. While it offers high-density memory and a powerful NVIDIA H100 GPU, the CPU allocation is shared, and there is no local storage included. This configuration is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that heavily leverage GPU acceleration and large memory capacities without requiring dedicated CPU cores or local NVMe drives. It is highly suited for deep learning, LLM inference, data science, and memory-intensive GPU-accelerated computing.
